_comment: PICKUP-GLOW. The one highlight every world pickup shares. Owner playtest 2026-08-30, OP-0830-3: 'all items in the grass like tms, potions, orbs whatever should glow so they're visible.' See scripts/world/pickup_glow.gd for the mechanism and shaders/pickup_glow.gdshader for why it is shaped this way. ALL OF THIS IS TUNABLE; `enabled` false is the whole revert.
_comment_scope: Every pickup path registers: harvest_node.gd (the gathering nodes -- 114 of them across the five bands), key_pickup.gd (the castle gate key and the Sunstone), tm_pickup.gd, item_cache_pickup.gd, felled_resource.gd (what a chopped tree leaves on the ground) and death_satchel.gd. A sixth path that forgets to call `PICKUP_GLOW.attach` is what tests/test_pickup_glow.gd exists to catch.
_comment_mote: The 'something is here' cue: a soft camera-facing halo on the object itself. OWNER DIRECTIVES, 2026-08-30: 'glow on the actual item, not floating in the air above it' and 'don't make it take over the items actual geometry or design. just add the glow to them.' Both are structural, not cosmetic. The first killed an earlier version that hung the mark at a fixed 1.15m to clear the grass -- correct about grass, wrong about everything else, because a light hovering over an object is a waypoint marker rather than an object that glows. The second is why `behind` exists: a camera-facing quad centred on a small prop paints straight over it, so the player sees a bright disc where the object used to be. Pushing the quad `behind` metres away from the camera lets the item's own opaque geometry occlude the middle of its glow, so only the halo escapes around its silhouette and the item is still drawn whole.
_comment_mote_placement: `body_fraction` is where on the prop the halo centres -- 0.55 of its measured crown, so a 20cm TM orb glows through its own middle and a two-metre deadwood pile glows through its trunk rather than over its head. `height` is only the fallback for a prop with no measurable mesh, and `max_height` is the ceiling that stops a tall prop's mark drifting up off the object it belongs to. Grass is then beaten by RADIUS: a halo this wide centred low still reaches above grass_field.json's ~0.86m canopy, but it reaches up OUT OF the object instead of hovering over it, which is the whole difference the owner asked for. tests/test_pickup_glow.gd asserts that reach against grass_field.json directly, so the ground lane raising blade height still fails loudly and names the number to move.
_comment_aura: The 'it is exactly HERE' cue, and the reason the mote alone is not enough: a mote high enough to clear grass is by definition not where the item is, so without this the player walks to a floating light and then hunts at their feet. A flat additive disc at the object's base bleeds into the blade bottoms and puts the find back on the ground. Bigger and much softer than the mote on purpose -- it is a wash, not a second marker. `pulse_depth` 0 keeps it steady while the mote breathes, so the pair does not read as one flashing object.
_comment_tint: How an item's colour becomes a glow colour. `data/items/items.json` authors ALBEDO -- `wood` is #7a5a35, `stone` is #8e8d86 -- and those are correct for a surface and useless as additive light: a dark brown added to a frame is nearly nothing. So the HUE stays the object's (a fiber node reads green, the gate key reads gold) and the BRIGHTNESS is this system's. `saturation_max` is a CAP, not a floor, on purpose: forcing a minimum saturation would assign a genuinely grey item an arbitrary hue off a channel that means nothing at zero saturation, and a stone deposit glowing pink is worse than one glowing warm white. TUNABLE; lower `value` for a subtler world, raise `saturation_max` for more colour separation between item types.
_comment_distance: Distance compensation, shared by both layers. A fixed-size world quad is a dinner plate at 2m and a sub-pixel speck at 40m, which is exactly backwards -- the far case is the one the owner reported. `reference_distance` is where the authored radius is used unscaled; nearer and further it is scaled toward a constant SCREEN size, clamped by `screen_min_scale`/`screen_max_scale` so it neither vanishes up close nor becomes a tree-sized billboard at range. `far_fade_*` is where it arrives from nothing rather than popping in. `near_fade_*` and `near_floor` are the anti-loot-beam rule: inside a few metres the player can SEE the object, so the glow steps down to `near_floor` of itself and gets out of the way rather than washing out the thing it was pointing at. It never goes to zero -- an item at your feet in tall grass is still the case being solved.
